subject: Money
title: Signaling with Money
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Signaling with Money.

hook.text: A Rolex costs $10,000. It tells time as well as a $30 Casio. You're not buying timekeeping.

buildup.text: Thorstein Veblen coined 'conspicuous consumption' in 1899. Spending to display wealth, not to use goods.

discovery.text: Signaling theory: expensive things prove you can afford waste. The waste itself is the message.

twist.text: Stealth wealth is rising. The truly rich now signal by not signaling. Plain clothes, no logos.

climax.text: Spending to signal is a tax on insecurity. Confidence doesn't need a receipt.

punchline.text: Buy the watch for you. Not for them.
